ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN List, and domestic law-enforcement financial intelligence indicators. Politically Exposed Persons are defined as individuals entrusted with prominent public functions domestically or internationally, including their family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP status, complex ownership structures, cross-border high-risk jurisdictions, and any adverse media or sanctions match. Verification and UBO identification must be completed before incorporation and updated on an ongoing risk-sensitive basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - New Zealand Companies Register (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be registrable in Latin-script form; English and Maori names are accepted, while non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. The legal name must include a limited-liability suffix such as 'Limited' or 'Ltd', and must not be identical or almost identical to an existing reserved or registered name, nor likely to mislead or cause confusion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Apply through the Companies Office online portal for a name reservation extension before the initial 20-working-day period expires; one extension of 20 working days is permitted. If the proposed name is rejected, file a formal reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 20 workings day of the refusal, attaching the original application, the reason for rejection, and a written submission addressing why the name is not likely to mislead, offensive, or contrary to law. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, judicial review may be sought in the High Court of New Zealand under the Senior Courts Act 2016 and the Judicature Amendment Act 1972.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office service that provides a physical street address within New Zealand and accepts service of legal documents is permissible. A PO Box, virtual reception-only address, or address without a physical street presence does not satisfy the registered office requirement. No physical business premises are mandated for a low-risk ISIC 6201 mobile utility software company operating through app-store sales.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: less than 5% probability of an unannounced physical inspection in the first year for a non-licensed, low-risk mobile software company, absent AML/CFT suspicion, adverse filing history, or a regulatory complaint.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No. 105), particularly sections 5, 12, 15, 20, 21, 22, 118, 124, 125, 126, 151, 152, 184, 189, 194; Companies (Incorporation) Regulations 2001; Financial Reporting Act 2013; Income Tax Act 2007.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), online registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company under Section 12 of the Companies Act 1993, filed through the Companies Office online incorporation system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under New Zealand law. Shares may be issued with no par value, and the consideration fixed by the board; no escrow account, capital lock-up, or paid-up capital deposit requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability and Legal Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — online company name search and reservation function.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or closely similar to an existing registered name. Ensure the selected name does not create a false impression of Crown ownership, official status, or misleading industry designation. The name must end with a restricted word such as Limited or its approved abbreviation, unless an exemption applies.
required_dossiers: No statutory dossier is required for a name search.
Where the name is similar to an existing entity, a written consent letter from the prior name holder is required.
Brief descriptive memorandum explaining the proposed name and business scope, if queried by the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a revised incorporation application using an alternative name; if an objection is raised by a third party, file a written response with distinguished factual submissions, or seek the objecting party’s written consent and resubmit the application within the statutory response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitutional Documents and Initial Officer Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial shareholders, directors, and legal advisers acting privately; no registry filing is required for the constitution unless the company opts to file it.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a constitution or rely on the default rules in the Companies Act 1993. Obtain signed consent to act as director from each proposed director and shareholder consent to share allotment. Record the proposed directors’ full legal names, residential addresses, and directorships held in New Zealand. Confirm share sub-classes, voting rights, or transfer restrictions are compatible with proposed mobile utility app commercial model.
required_dossiers: Constitution, if adopted.
Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director.
Written shareholder consent to the initial share subscription.
Director identification documentation (passport and proof of residential address), notarized where necessary.
Statement of share issue and proposed paid-up or unpaid conditions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defect in the consent or identity documentation; obtain a fresh signature or sworn statutory declaration under the Oaths and Declarations Act 1957 where identity verification is questioned; reissue board consent forms if any materially erroneous statement is discovered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Application for Registration to the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — online ‘Incorporate a Company’ portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Companies Office online portal, enter the verified company name, registered office address, address for service, directors, shareholders, share structure, and NZ residential details of directors. Complete the statutory declaration that all statements are true, pay the prescribed filing fee electronically, and submit the application for screening. Ensure at least one director is a natural person who is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, or that a valid alternate director arrangement exists under the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Name availability confirmation or consent letter.
Completed Application for Registration of a Company under section 12.
Signed consent to act as director for each named director.
Registered office and address for service details in New Zealand.
Electronically verified director identification documents.
Prescribed filing fee paid by credit card, debit card, or online transfer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or refused, review the registry notice, correct the specified defect, and resubmit; if the rejection rests on a name conflict, file a fresh application under an alternative approved name; if the Registrar rejects on substantive grounds, seek reconsideration through the Companies Office contact channel or judicial review before the High Court under section 364 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Registrar of Companies issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation. The company becomes a legal entity from the date stated on the certificate. The NZBN is automatically allocated and registered in the New Zealand Business Register. Immediately prepare internal statutory registers including the share register, director register, registered office records, and in-progress minute book as required by sections 187 and 194 of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar.
New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) confirmation.
Initial share register and register of directors.
Registered office address confirmation.
Corporate file and seal, if adopted by the board.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate address or entity details contain a clerical error, request a formal amendment via the Companies Office’s ‘Correct a Grievous’ or correction process; if the certificate goes astray, apply for a certified copy of the incorporation certificate by filing the appropriate statutory request and paying the applicable verification fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Taxation and Statutory Governance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) via NZBN login to myIR online services; New Zealand Companies Office for annual returns.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NZBN to authenticate the company with Inland Revenue, register for income tax, and obtain an IRD number. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) if taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period, or if voluntary GST registration is desired. If the company will employ staff, register as an employer for PAYE. Maintain shareholder and director registers, prepare financial statements under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, and file the first annual return with the Companies Office within the prescribed statutory period.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation.
NZBN number.
Registered office and director details.
Projected taxable supply volume for GST registration.
Bank account details for tax refunds and IRD payments.
Financial statements and auditor-report requirements, if applicable under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is delayed or rejected, verify the company’s legal details with the Companies Office and resubmit through myIR with corrected documentation; if the IRD queries GST or income tax thresholds, provide supporting projection and board minute; if a dispute arises, issue a Notice of Response to IRD within the statutory response period and use available escalation channels under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing authority is prescribed for ISIC 6201 software and mobile utility application development. General business regulatory oversight is exercised by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) and WorkSafe New Zealand, while local territorial authorities administer building and fire-occupancy consents.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no government operating permit or manufacturing license is required for a mobile utility software publishing business. Commercial distribution is governed by the Apple Developer Program License Agreement and the Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement, which are contract frameworks and not statutory licensing instruments.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure software development and digital publishing operations entail no physical land-use change, industrial installation, or discharge; no Environmental Impact Assessment is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the economic activity itself, as no point-source wastewater, VOC, or production waste stream is generated. Any office-origin waste must be consigned through municipal disposal systems under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; if work is conducted in leased premises, the tenant must comply with the landlord’s health and safety and building-systems obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance is required under the Building Act 2004 for any occupied office premises: a Building Warrant of Fitness (BWOF) must be current where specified systems such as fire alarms, automatic sprinklers, or mechanical ventilation are present. Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) requires an evacuation scheme to be approved and maintained where staff numbers exceed statutory thresholds. WorkSafe New Zealand and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 mandate hazard identification, worker engagement, welfare facilities, and notifiable event reporting. Local territorial authority consent for building use and structural load inspections must be confirmed by the landlord or tenant before ongoing office operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake; secure taxpayer portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz). Supporting registries: New Zealand Companies Office (NZBN for registered companies) and New Zealand Customs Service (export declarations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Confirm non-resident status: under s YC 15 Income Tax Act 2007, a company is New Zealand tax-resident if it is incorporated in New Zealand or if its centre of management (control and management of the business) is exercised in New Zealand. The CK_IC is an overseas-incorporated International Company; provided central management and control remains offshore, it is a non-resident company. 2. A non-resident company that does not carry on a taxable activity in New Zealand and has no New Zealand-sourced income has no statutory obligation to hold an IRD number. 3. To register for GST (whether compulsorily or voluntarily under s 51(3) GST Act 1986), the company applies to Inland Revenue by: (a) obtaining an IRD income-tax number using form IR742 ('IRD number application - non-resident company'); and (b) submitting form IR747 ('GST registration - non-resident company') together with documents evidencing the taxable activity (App Store seller agreements, revenue projections for New Zealand consumers, marketplace operator confirmation). 4. If the entity later establishes a New Zealand branch and registers as an overseas company on the Companies Register, it obtains an NZBN and completes IRD/GST registration through myIR; ongoing income tax and GST returns are filed electronically via myIR. 5. The effective GST registration date is the date of commencement of the taxable activity or the date the NZD 60,000 threshold is exceeded, and registration may not be backdated beyond statutory limits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident International Company without a New Zealand permanent establishment and without New Zealand-sourced income; New Zealand income-tax neutrality for offshore App Store revenue; GST exposure limited to New Zealand-consumer remote-service supplies, generally collected by the marketplace operator).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid entity classification election exists in New Zealand. Entity tax treatment is determined by statute under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the CFC/FIF rules; a foreign entity is classified according to its foreign legal status and New Zealand source taxation principles. Statutory elections available to a non-resident company include: (i) voluntary GST registration under s 51(3) GST Act 1986; (ii) GST group registration under s 55 GST Act 1986 (with a New Zealand-resident group member); (iii) functional-currency election for financial arrangements under s DN 2 Income Tax Act 2007, subject to IRD consent; and (iv) hybrid and branch mismatch neutralisation is applied automatically under subpart FH (Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018) without an elective check-the-box mechanism. The look-through company (LTC) election is unavailable because the entity is non-resident and LTC status requires a New Zealand-resident close-held company.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - New Zealand's consumption-type value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (GST registration threshold for any person carrying on a taxable activity in any 12-month period; the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to offshore suppliers of remote services and low-value goods supplied to New Zealand consumers). Supplies of mobile utility apps to New Zealand consumers through Apple App Store / Google Play are generally treated as made by the marketplace operator, which collects GST at 15%; the underlying non-resident developer may therefore remain below the registration threshold where all sales are effected through such marketplaces.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-approval, or digital stamping regime. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the PEPPOL network through certified service providers; invoices must nevertheless satisfy the GST tax-invoice content requirements (s 24 GST Act 1986) and be retained for 7 years. GST returns and payments are filed electronically through myIR; no API-based fiscal-authority pre-clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: s 11 GST Act 1986 zero-rates goods that the supplier exports, provided the goods are exported within 28 days of the time of supply and the supplier holds prescribed export evidence. Services/digital products: s 11A/11B zero-rate services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land or goods physically present in New Zealand; services performed wholly outside New Zealand are zero-rated. For mobile utility apps sold through Apple App Store / Google Play: the developer's supply to the non-resident marketplace operator is zero-rated as a remote service to a non-resident, while the marketplace operator is deemed to make the supply to New Zealand consumers and must charge 15% GST. To substantiate zero-rating, the developer must retain evidence of the marketplace operator's non-resident status, the app-store distribution agreements, and settlement/payout reports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (lodged via Trade Single Window / New Zealand Customs Service)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (evidencing physical export within 28 days of supply under s 11(1)(b) GST Act 1986)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advices (evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the recognised repatriation window)
Commercial Invoice and detailed Packing List
Certificate of Origin (only where preferential origin treatment is claimed)
Digital-services substantiation pack (app-store settlement reports, marketplace operator contracts, recipient non-residency evidence, and IP ownership records)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reopen GST assessments within the statutory time bar (generally 4 years from the end of the relevant GST period) and claw back any zero-rated refund together with use-of-money interest where export evidence is deficient or the statutory zero-rating criteria are not met. Shortfall penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for an unacceptable tax position or failure to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness (abusive tax position), and 150% for evasion or fraudulent intent. Fraudulent GST evasion also carries criminal liability (fines and/or imprisonment). Exporters must retain all zero-rating supporting records for 7 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), operating under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as conduct regulator; New Zealand maintains a freely floating exchange-rate regime with no centralised exchange-control authority or foreign-investment approval body for standard trade transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility, having accepted Article VIII obligations of the IMF Articles of Agreement. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) floats freely, and there are no statutory barriers to the repatriation of dividends, capital, loan repayments, or distributed profits by non-resident shareholders of a New Zealand-incorporated International Company. Digital service export revenue, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlements, is fully convertible without ministerial consent; the only practical frictions are tax withholding obligations (NRWT/RWT), AML/CFT reporting thresholds, and standard correspondent-bank compliance procedures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligations. There is no mandatory statutory timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no requirement to deposit export receipts into a specified domestic account. Cross-border digital app-store earnings received in USD, EUR, and other foreign currencies may be retained indefinitely in multi-currency operational accounts, segregated into capital escrow sub-accounts, or sold on the open market at prevailing commercial rates without any Reserve Bank notification or licence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account with segregated Capital Escrow sub-account
Operational account with nested Capital Escrow ledger; strong API and treasury functionality
Operational account and separate Capital Escrow cash-management account
Operational clearing account with multi-currency sweep; deep correspondent-banking network
Operational NZD account; limited multi-currency and treasury hedging capability
Operational retail-grade account; minimal cross-border treasury infrastructure

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as a primary or sole banking relationship. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex) are not registered banks in New Zealand, are not members of the Reserve Bank's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESB), and cannot provide NZD settlement finality or local clearing. They are viable strictly as auxiliary cross-border payment and FX-conversion corridors for app-store payouts, subject to the core treasury and escrow balances being held with an NZ registered bank. Legal constraints include the absence of deposit-taking authorisation under the Deposit Takers Act 2023 and the application of enhanced due diligence when EMI channel funding originates from jurisdictions without equivalent AML/CFT regimes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT law does not mandate physical appearance of directors; account opening may lawfully proceed through electronic identity verification (EIV), certified documentary packs, and video-conference KYC interviews. In practice, tier-1 domestic banks permit fully remote onboarding for a low-risk International Company with non-resident ownership, provided directors submit notarised passport copies, proof of residential address, corporate registers, and a tax-residence certificate; a virtual interview is routinely required. Banks may impose an in-person visit or require a New Zealand-based chartered accountant or law-firm introducer where the beneficial ownership chain involves trust structures or high-risk jurisdictions, but such physical presence is a policy overlay rather than a statutory mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company structure flagged as a potential shell or pass-through vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Constitution; full Register of Directors and Shareholders; beneficial ownership schedule; economic-substance memorandum detailing active mobile-utility software development, server hosting, and user-support operations; audited or internally prepared financial statements; board resolution authorising the bank relationship; commercial contracts with app-store distributors and software developers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and zero-tax classification misinterpreted as tax evasion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IRD tax-status confirmation or exemption certificate; written tax advice memorandum from a licensed New Zealand tax advisor; corporate legal opinion on the permitted activities and tax neutrality of the International Company; up-to-date corporate filings; documented dividend and capital repatriation policy consistent with transfer-pricing standards; CRS and FATCA registration attestations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: App-store freemium revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing with no physical retail footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; App Store Connect and Google Play Console administrative access; monthly payout and settlement statements from Apple and Google; application warehouse code ownership evidence; mobile-utility performance data and user-acquisition metrics; merchant agreements with payment processors; domain and trademark registrations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner concealed behind a Cayman Islands (CK) interposed holding vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share-register extracts of the CK parent; trust deed or foundation deed where applicable; registry-issued certificate of good standing; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; bank reference letters from the CK parent's financiers; chain-of-ownership diagram through to human beneficial owners; confirmations that the CK entity is not subject to adverse sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection without contemporaneous commercial rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription and allotment resolution; board minutes explaining commercial purpose (development capital, IP acquisition, working capital); executed capital contribution agreement; SWIFT MT103 confirmation and bank reference; cash-flow forecast for the mobile utility application; external audit confirmation of the capital movement in the next financial statements; appointment of a compliance officer or money-laundering reporting officer for the account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital routing utilises the SWIFT MT103 wire protocol from the CK parent's corporate bank to the NZ IC's operational or capital-escrow account, referencing the appropriate Balance of Payments (BOP) purpose code for direct-investment equity injection. The beneficiary NZ bank performs 'name and account' matching against the profile, applies automatic suspicious-transaction reporting for cash-equivalent instruments, and initiates Enhanced Customer Due Diligence (ECDD) for injections exceeding NZD 50,000. The verification dossier must accompany the wire as a scanned payment instruction: share-allotment board resolution, source-of-funds bank statement, certificate of incorporation of the remitter, ultimate beneficial owner declaration, and an import/export or service contract if the capital is linked to future app monetisation. Where the injection exceeds NZD 500,000, banks may require a pre-approval notice and a clearing-certificate from the correspondent bank; funds are credited only after finality is received through the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESB), not on provisional advice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements clear through layered rails: SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier wires; Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits subject to UCP600) for hardware procurement and IP-licence acquisitions; and domestic NZD payments via the Reserve Bank's ESB through the clearing member bank. App-store settlement proceeds from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are received via Apple's and Google's global treasury rails in USD, EUR, or local currencies into the NZ IC's multi-currency account, then pooled and converted into NZD through same-day FX swaps for operating disbursements. Aggregate settlement is consolidated in a concentration account with same-day value dating; enterprise B2B invoices are issued through electronic banking ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002 flows, and recurring treasury sweeps reconcile the capital escrow ledger against share-capital records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (vanilla outright forwards in NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/AUD) booked under a master FX agreement with the NZ clearing bank

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) strictly limited to hedging illiquid emerging-market currency balances accumulated from non-NZD app-store payout jurisdictions; NZD itself is fully deliverable and therefore not subject to NDF treatment
Cross-Currency Swaps (fixed-floating and fixed-fixed swaps) to manage tenor-matched conversion risk on intercompany funding and dividend streams
FX Swaps (swap of principal and interest in two currencies) used for short-term liquidity management between capital-escrow and operational ledgers
Vanilla OTC Currency Options (plain-vanilla calls and puts on NZD crosses) purchased for downside protection with unlimited upside on app-store revenue conversion
Collateralised Currency Swaps under an ISDA Credit Support Annex (CSA) executed only with a registered New Zealand bank to satisfy margin rules and avoid speculative hedging prohibition

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (AR) of the International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: annual return date is the last day of the month of incorporation (e.g., 30 September for a September-incorporated company); return must be filed on or before that date; a statutory tolerance of one month applies before default procedures commence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a compliance notice and an offence liability of up to NZD 10,000 (approximately USD 6,100) for the company and each director; after six months in arrears the Registrar may apply to remove the company from the register under section 325 Companies Act 1993, whereupon its property vests in the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements and statutory audit report (filed if the entity is 'large' or audit is shareholder-requested)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after balance date (standard balance date 31 March; statements due by 31 August). Sub-threshold entities (small companies) are exempt from filing unless shareholder(s) holding at least 5% of voting rights request an audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For a large company, late or non-filing is an offence carrying fines up to NZD 10,000 (approximately USD 6,100); persistent default permits removal from the register and loss of limited liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company income tax return (IR4) for a non-resident / tax-exempt international company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue (Inland Revenue Department; myIR portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after balance date (e.g., by 30 September for a 31 March balance date); a nil IR4 plus supporting non-resident schedule is filed to evidence the tax-exempt status.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 (approximately USD 153); use-of-money interest accrues on any assessed liability; continued default allows IRD to issue assessments and enforce recovery, including attachment orders and referral for deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of share allotment and notification of director/registered-office changes (annual register reconciliation event)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days of each event; the resulting register data is reconciled and certified in the next annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-notification is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 with fines up to NZD 10,000 (approximately USD 6,100); stale registers may invalidate reliance on the register and accelerate removal proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies only where (a) the company is 'large' under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 - exceeding at least two of: total assets NZD 60 million; total revenue NZD 30 million; 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees - for two consecutive accounting periods; (b) shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights deliver a written audit request; or (c) the company qualifies as an FMC reporting entity. A freemium mobile-utility app entity with no public offer of securities does not meet these thresholds and is exempt from audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents of IFRS (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1; NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (RDR) for Tier 2 for-profit entities; or NZ GAAP (XRB A1) for non-publicly-accountable small entities. The App-Store company typically reports as a Tier 2 for-profit small company under the External Reporting Board (XRB) framework.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not grant general statutory tax holidays. For an International Company (CK_IC) structured as a non-resident-owned tax-exempt entity, no New Zealand corporate income tax applies on foreign-sourced income provided the company has no New Zealand permanent establishment or fixed establishment. The R&D tax credit (15% of eligible expenditure) and software depreciation deductions can lower the effective rate on any New Zealand-sourced taxable income. Fully imputed dividends are effectively taxed at the corporate rate through the imputation credit system.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or by a tax agent; provisional and terminal tax payments are also managed via myIR.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed by the 7th month after the company's balance date (e.g., 31 October for a 31 March balance date). Provisional tax is due in three instalments: 7th and 11th months of the income year, and the 7th month following year-end (terminal tax).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: all assessable income derived by the company during the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident International Company without a permanent establishment, include only New Zealand-source income; foreign app-store revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing is excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit: income less deductible expenses, adjusted for apportionment of expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only to the extent they relate to New Zealand-source income; apportion costs such as development and marketing expenses if they relate to both New Zealand and foreign sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: net profit adjusted by tax adjustments (e.g., non-deductible amounts and transfer pricing add-backs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an exempt IC with no New Zealand-source income, enter zero. Include add-backs for any transfer pricing adjustments under s GC 6 of the Income Tax Act 2007.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax liability: calculated at 28% of taxable income, less available credits (imputation, R&D, foreign tax credits, etc.).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 28% rate only to New Zealand-source non-withholding income. Dividends, interest, and royalties are generally subject to final NRWT or AIL and not included here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: provisional tax paid, RWT, or other credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are limited to New Zealand tax payable; foreign tax credits only apply under a double tax agreement to the same New Zealand-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: NZ$250 (small/medium) or NZ$500 (large) initial penalty, plus NZ$4 per day thereafter, capped at NZ$250/NZ$500. Late payment triggers use-of-money interest (currently ~8.34% per annum) and shortfall penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-residents. The approved issuer levy (AIL) applies to interest at 2% in certain circumstances.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate under the New Zealand–Cook Islands DTA, the non-resident recipient must provide a certificate of residence (IR290) or a tax residence certificate (TRC) from the Cook Islands competent authority to the New Zealand payer before payment. The payer then withholds at the treaty rate (dividends generally 15%, interest 10%, royalties 10%). Inland Revenue requires the certificate to be retained; over-withheld amounts can be claimed by filing a return within 4 years of the income year.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT rates: interest 15%, royalties 15%. Under the NZ–Cook Islands DTA, the source-country rate is capped at 10% for both interest and royalties. For related-party interest, New Zealand's thin capitalisation rules may restrict deductions if net debt exceeds 60% of total assets for a non-resident-owned company. AIL at 2% can replace NRWT on registered, arm's-length interest paid to unrelated non-residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local file documentation required for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZ$10 million in total, or NZ$1 million for transactions involving services, interest, royalties, or intangibles. Master file required for multinational groups with annual revenue over NZ$100 million and cross-border related-party transactions above those thresholds. Country-by-Country reporting applies where group revenue exceeds EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate separate Economic Substance Regulations like the UAE or BVI. Instead, the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1, Income Tax Act 2007) and transfer pricing rules (s GC 6) deny tax benefits where an International Company lacks substantive presence and real decision-making in its claimed jurisdiction of residence. For a mobile utility app (ISIC 6201), the IP owner must perform DEMPE functions (development, enhancement, maintenance, protection, exploitation) with actual personnel and decision-making where the IP returns are booked. The BEPS Multilateral Instrument's principal purpose test may also deny treaty benefits under the NZ–Cook Islands DTA if obtaining treaty relief was the primary purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Rerouting Apple IAP and Google Play Billing profits to the Cook Islands International Company while New Zealand employees and directors continue to make all substantive decisions and perform the app development functions, without arm's-length compensation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR applies: the Commissioner re-characterises the arrangement and assesses the full New Zealand-source income at 28%, plus use-of-money interest. Shortfall penalty: 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion, 40% for unacceptable tax position, 20% for lack of reasonable care. Criminal conviction for evasion can result in imprisonment up to 4 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in or directing the evasion can be personally prosecuted under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (fine up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years). They are liable for company debts under the Companies Act 1993 if the company trades recklessly or fraudulently, and may face departure prohibition orders, asset restraint, and personal restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the CK_IC as a nominee shell with no office, staff, bank account, or records, while claiming offshore royalty income from the app's intellectual property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The entity may be disregarded as a sham; the New Zealand Inland Revenue can assess the underlying economic activity in New Zealand and deny DTA benefits under the principal purpose test. Penalties: 40% unacceptable tax position or 150% evasion penalty, plus interest and recharacterisation of all distributions as taxable dividends subject to NRWT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced: directors are personally liable for tax debts, unlawful distributions, and fraudulent trading. The High Court may order repayment of revenue and punitive damages; directors face travel bans, personal bankruptcy, and extradition for serious tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving app payments via App Store rails without adequate customer due diligence on the merchant/beneficiary, failing to maintain AML records, or using shell accounts to obscure the ultimate beneficial owner where the entity is in scope of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to NZ$10 million for a body corporate and NZ$200,000 for individuals; criminal liability for money laundering under the Crimes Act 1961 carries imprisonment up to 7 years. Financial Intelligence Unit may freeze accounts and restrain proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers are individually liable for breaches of the AML/CFT programme; criminal convictions can lead to imprisonment up to 7 years and fines. Management bans up to 10 years may be imposed, and directors may be personally liable for civil penalties for losses caused to creditors or beneficiaries.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for intercompany royalty or profit-split arrangements for the app's IP, particularly where cross-border related-party service transactions exceed NZ$1 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Commissioner may adjust the taxable profits to arm's length, disallow intercompany deductions, and impose a 20% shortfall penalty for non-documentation (or higher for gross carelessness or evasion). The taxpayer bears the burden of proof without documentation. Penalties can reach 150% of the shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign returns without reasonable basis face personal penalty risk, including a 100% penalty for gross carelessness under s 141A or 150% for evasion. They may be personally liable for breaches of director duties under the Companies Act 1993, be required to restore misapplied amounts, and be disqualified from management.
